answer: Disjoint Path Relay Quorum. An action is accepted only when it reaches validators over three edge-disjoint paths through distinct relay neighborhoods within a rolling window. Paths that converge on shared relays hit a topology nadir and are rate-limited. An attacker must rent and keep live separate relays in each neighborhood, paying per identity for unique links, uptime, and latency. That cost scales with path count, so bulk identities lose their haven. A node reaches the summit only after sustained path diversity, not volume.
